settings.title: Knowledge store
settings.summary: Where Keystone keeps what it remembers between chats.
settings.description: The knowledge store Keystone remembers in. With none, Keystone keeps your chats and remembers nothing between them. The built-in store keeps what it remembers in your own Keystone folder. Waymarks is your own Waymarks instance, at the address and with the tokens you give.

settings.title: Waymarks address
settings.summary: Where your Waymarks instance is.
settings.description: Where your Waymarks instance is, such as http://127.0.0.1:7878. Its tokens are kept with your secrets and never here.

settings.title: Waymarks time limit
settings.summary: How long Keystone waits for an answer from Waymarks.
settings.description: How long Keystone waits for one answer from Waymarks before it carries on without it, from 100ms to 2m.

settings.title: Waymarks search results
settings.summary: The most results one search of Waymarks returns.
settings.description: The most results one search of Waymarks returns when the search names no limit, from 1 to 100.

settings.title: Waymarks vector batch
settings.summary: The most pages asked of Waymarks at once when making vectors.
settings.description: The most pages Keystone asks Waymarks for at once when it lists the pages needing a vector, from 1 to 1000.

settings.title: Waymarks answer size
settings.summary: The largest answer Keystone reads from Waymarks.
settings.description: The largest answer Keystone reads from Waymarks, in megabytes, from 1 to 1024. A larger one is treated as Waymarks being unavailable.

settings.title: Built-in search results
settings.summary: The most results one search of the built-in store returns.
settings.description: The most results one search of the built-in knowledge store returns when the search names no limit, from 1 to 1000.

settings.title: Built-in search excerpt
settings.summary: About how many words of a match each built-in result shows.
settings.description: About how many words of a matching page or source a result from the built-in knowledge store shows, from 1 to 64.

settings.title: Built-in vector batch
settings.summary: The most pages the built-in store lists at once for vectors.
settings.description: The most pages the built-in knowledge store lists at once as needing a vector, from 1 to 10000.

settings.title: Profile length
settings.summary: The longest a person's profile may be.
settings.description: The longest a person's profile may be, in characters, from 1 to 20000. The profile starts every call to a model, so a longer one costs more on every message.

settings.title: Knowledge map size
settings.summary: The most room the map of your knowledge may take in a call.
settings.description: The most room the map of your knowledge store may take at the start of a call, in tokens, from 0 to 20000. A map that would be larger shows fewer titles, then fewer kinds of page, then fewer spaces. With 0 no map is sent.

settings.title: Titles in the map
settings.summary: How many page titles the map shows under each kind of page.
settings.description: How many page titles the map of your knowledge store shows under each kind of page, from 0 to 20. With 0 it shows the kinds and their counts alone.

settings.title: Map title length
settings.summary: The longest a name or title is shown in the map.
settings.description: The longest a space's name, a kind of page or a page title is shown in the map of a knowledge store, in characters, from 8 to 200. A longer one is cut.

settings.title: Recall
settings.summary: Searches your knowledge with each message and tells the model what it finds.
settings.description: Whether Keystone searches your knowledge store with each message you send and gives the model what it finds. With no knowledge store nothing is searched either way.

settings.title: Recall time limit
settings.summary: How long recall may take before a reply starts without it.
settings.description: How long recall may take before a reply starts without it, from 100ms to 1m. A knowledge store that is slow or down never stops a chat.

settings.title: Relevance bar, built-in store
settings.summary: How relevant a built-in page must be to be recalled.
settings.description: The relevance threshold for recall from the built-in knowledge store. A page or source that scores lower for your message is left out. The score is the store's own ranking: in a store of a few dozen pages or more, a word that few pages hold scores about 1 or more, and a word that half the pages hold scores close to 0. With 0 everything the search finds may be recalled, which is right for a small store.

settings.title: Relevance bar, Waymarks
settings.summary: How relevant a Waymarks page must be to be recalled.
settings.description: The relevance threshold for recall from Waymarks. A page or source that scores lower for your message is left out. The score is on Waymarks' own scale. With 0 everything the search finds may be recalled.

settings.title: Recall by meaning
settings.summary: Recall also searches by meaning, not only by words.
settings.description: Whether recall searches your knowledge store by meaning as well as by words. It does when you have an embedding model and the store takes a vector to search with. Off, or with neither, recall searches by words alone.

settings.title: Pages found by meaning
settings.summary: The most pages a search by meaning adds to recall.
settings.description: The most pages a search by meaning finds for your message, which join what the search by words found, from 1 to 100.

settings.title: Meaning bar, built-in store
settings.summary: How close in meaning a built-in page must be to be recalled.
settings.description: The relevance threshold for a page the built-in store finds by meaning. Its score is the cosine between the page's vector and your message's, from 0 to 1. A page that scores lower is left out.

settings.title: Meaning bar, Waymarks
settings.summary: How close in meaning a Waymarks page must be to be recalled.
settings.description: The relevance threshold for a page Waymarks finds by meaning. Waymarks scores a search by vector by its place in the list, not by how near it is, so with 0 every page it finds by meaning may be recalled.

settings.title: Weight of word matches
settings.summary: How much word matches count when the two searches are merged.
settings.description: How much a page's place in the search by words counts when it is merged with the search by meaning, from 0 to 100. With 0, the merged order is the meaning's.

settings.title: Weight of meaning matches
settings.summary: How much meaning matches count when the two searches are merged.
settings.description: How much a page's place in the search by meaning counts when it is merged with the search by words, from 0 to 100. With 0, the merged order is the words'. Both cannot be 0.

settings.title: Merge constant
settings.summary: How much the top places count when the two searches are merged.
settings.description: The constant k in the merge of the two searches: a page scores weight / (k + its place) in each, summed. The larger it is, the less the first places count above the later ones, from 1 to 1000. 60 is what Waymarks' own hybrid search uses.

settings.title: Prepare pages for meaning search
settings.summary: Makes vectors of your pages so recall can search by meaning.
settings.description: Whether Keystone makes vectors of the pages in your knowledge store, in the background, so recall can search them by meaning. It does when you have an embedding model and the store takes vectors.

settings.title: Vector batch size
settings.summary: How many pages go to the embedding model in one call.
settings.description: How many pages go to the embedding model in one call, from 1 to 256.

settings.title: Pages in one refresh
settings.summary: The most pages one vector refresh handles.
settings.description: The most pages one refresh of a person's vectors sends to the embedding model, from 1 to 100000. The rest wait for the next refresh.

settings.title: Pages listed for a refresh
settings.summary: The most pages a vector refresh asks the store to list.
settings.description: The most pages a refresh asks the knowledge store to list as needing a vector, from 1 to 100000. It is larger than the pages per refresh, because pages in a sensitive space a hosted embedding model may not read are listed too and passed over.

settings.title: Page text for vectors
settings.summary: How much of one page the embedding model is sent.
settings.description: The most characters of one page, its title and then its body, the embedding model is sent, from 100 to 1000000. A model whose window is smaller is sent less.

settings.title: Monthly budget for vectors
settings.summary: The most making vectors may spend in a month on paid models.
settings.description: The most making vectors may spend in a calendar month on embedding models that are not local, in US dollars: the refresh of your pages and the vector of each message recall searches with. It is a part of the monthly cap, not an addition to it. Zero keeps embeddings to local models.

settings.title: Vector refresh interval
settings.summary: How often Keystone looks for pages that need a new vector.
settings.description: How often Keystone looks for pages whose vector is missing or stale, because the page changed or the embedding model did, and makes new ones, from 1m to 24h.

settings.title: Vector time limit
settings.summary: How long one background call to the embedding model may take.
settings.description: How long one call to the embedding model may take in the background refresh, from 5s to 30m. The vector of a message is made inside recall's own time, knowledge.recall_timeout.

settings.title: Words recall ignores
settings.summary: Common words recall leaves out of its search.
settings.default: a about after again all also am an and any are as at be because been before being but by can could did do does doing done for from get got had has have having he her here hers him his how i if in into is it its just like me more most my no not now of off on one only or other our out over own please said say she should so some such tell than that the their them then there these they this those to too under up us very was we were what when where which while who why will with would yes you your
settings.description: Words recall leaves out when it searches your knowledge store with a message, separated by spaces. They are words that say nothing of what a message is about. A message made of them alone recalls nothing.

settings.title: Recall search results
settings.summary: How many results recall asks your knowledge store for.
settings.description: The most results recall asks your knowledge store for with each message, from 1 to 100, before the relevance threshold is applied.

settings.title: Items recalled
settings.summary: The most pages and sources recall gives a model with one message.
settings.description: The most pages and sources recall gives the model with one message, from 0 to 50. With 0 nothing is recalled.

settings.title: Recalled item length
settings.summary: How much of one recalled page the model is given.
settings.description: The most of one recalled page or source the model is given, in characters, from 100 to 100000. A longer one is cut, and the model can read the rest with a lookup.

settings.title: Message length for recall
settings.summary: How much of your message recall searches with.
settings.description: The most of your message recall searches with, in characters from its start, from 1 to 10000.

settings.title: Search-first rule
settings.summary: Tells the model to search your knowledge before it answers.
settings.default: This person keeps a knowledge store of their own. Before you answer anything about their world, or say you do not know, look in it. What Keystone found there for this message is given further down, when it found anything. When knowledge lookup tools are offered, search with them and read a page or a source in full. Say which page or source an answer came from.
settings.description: The search-first rule: what the standing instructions tell the model when you have a knowledge store. It is left out when you have none. Empty sends none.

settings.title: Remember from chats
settings.summary: After each reply, saves the lasting facts to your knowledge store.
settings.description: The memory pass: after each reply, a model reads what you wrote and the answer, and adds the durable facts it finds to your knowledge store, as a source that points back to the chat. It runs only when your store can take new sources, never in an incognito chat, and never delays a reply.

settings.title: Memory space
settings.summary: The space new facts from your chats are kept in.
settings.description: The space in your knowledge store the memory pass puts facts in. A space your store does not have yet is made, as a normal space.

settings.title: Sensitive memory space
settings.summary: The space for facts from chats that saw sensitive content.
settings.description: The space the memory pass puts facts in when the chat was sent content from a sensitive space. Your store must already have it, with a page in it, and say it is sensitive. Empty keeps such facts nowhere.

settings.title: Monthly budget for memory
settings.summary: The most remembering may spend in a month on paid models.
settings.description: The most the memory pass may spend in a calendar month on models that are not local, in US dollars. It is part of the monthly cap, not added to it, so the memory pass stops before it eats the cap. A local model costs nothing and is never stopped. Zero keeps the memory pass to local models.

settings.title: Memory instructions
settings.summary: What the model that picks out facts is told.
settings.default: You keep the long-term memory of a personal assistant. You are shown one exchange from a chat: what the person wrote and what the assistant answered. Write down the durable facts it shows about the person and their world: who they are, the people, places and things in their life, their projects, plans, habits, preferences and decisions, when they will still be true and useful in a later chat. Leave out what matters only to this conversation, what the assistant suggested that the person did not take up, general knowledge, and anything you are not sure of. Write each fact as one short sentence that stands on its own, and call the person "the person". Answer with one JSON object and nothing else, in this form: {"facts": ["...", "..."]}. Write at most {max} facts. When the exchange holds no durable fact, answer {"facts": []}.
settings.description: The instruction the memory pass's model is given with each exchange. {max} becomes the most facts it may write. The answer must stay one JSON object with a list of facts.

settings.title: Memory source name
settings.summary: How the source added for each reply is named.
settings.description: The name of the source the memory pass adds for one reply. {title} becomes the chat's title and {date} the day of the reply.

settings.title: Facts from one reply
settings.summary: The most facts kept from one reply.
settings.description: The most facts the memory pass keeps from one reply, from 1 to 100.

settings.title: Fact length
settings.summary: The longest fact that is kept.
settings.description: The longest fact the memory pass keeps, in characters, from 20 to 2000. A longer one is left out.

settings.title: Message length for memory
settings.summary: How much of a message and its reply the memory model is shown.
settings.description: The most of your message, and of the reply, the memory pass's model is shown, in characters, from 200 to 100000. A longer one is cut at a word's end.

settings.title: Memory output limit
settings.summary: The longest answer the memory model may write.
settings.description: The longest answer the memory pass's model may write, in tokens, from 64 to 32000.

settings.title: Memory time limit
settings.summary: How long remembering from one reply may take.
settings.description: How long one memory pass may take, its model call included, from 5s to 30m. A pass that runs out of time keeps nothing and says so in the server's log.

settings.title: Keep idle incognito chats
settings.summary: How long an idle incognito chat is kept before it is deleted.
settings.description: How long an incognito chat you have not left is kept once nothing more is said in it, from 5m to 720h. Then it is deleted with its messages, as it is at once when you leave it. Its model calls stay in the audit log, as every call does.

settings.title: Incognito clean-up interval
settings.summary: How often Keystone looks for incognito chats to delete.
settings.description: How often Keystone looks for incognito chats to delete: those you left, and those idle for longer than knowledge.incognito_keep. From 5s to 1h.

settings.title: Memories shown
settings.summary: The most remembered sources the Memory screen shows.
settings.description: The most sources the memory pass added that the Memory screen shows, the newest first, from 1 to 5000.

settings.title: Pages shown in each space
settings.summary: The most pages of each space the Memory screen lists.
settings.description: The most pages of each space the Memory screen lists, from 0 to 1000. The rest are counted.

settings.title: Lookup results
settings.summary: The most results a model's knowledge search returns.
settings.description: The most results one knowledge search by the model returns, from 1 to 100.

settings.title: Lookup length
settings.summary: How much text one knowledge lookup by a model returns.
settings.description: The most text one knowledge lookup by the model returns, in characters, from 200 to 200000. A longer page or source is read in parts.
